doc.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Philadelphia as a proving ground compared with New York
summary: Holley asks about Howard McGhee and the New York versus Philadelphia scenes; Heath calls Philadelphia a proving ground and Holley raises Coltrane.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: From that period, you talked about coming home and making the transition from being Lt. Heath to Percy Heath the bass player. And we talked about you playing with the great Howard McGhee, who really, in my opinion, is a very underrated musician. Was he responsible for bringing you to New York as a musician and can you contrast what it was like, what New York was to jazz and how your experiences there as a bass player were different than you being in Philly? Compare the jazz scene in New York and Philly.
Well, Philadelphia was like a proving ground. Many later to become famous musicians got their act together in Philadelphia.
And I wanted to say, did you also, you mentioned John Coltrane, did you play with John Coltrane when he was young, or did you see him develop when he was young?
